Subject: Recap & next steps: Dedicated GPU plan for MedAI (isolation + SLA)

Hi Samira & Victor —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from my side so we have alignment and clear next steps. I copied Evelyn and Karthik to pick up pricing and security items.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Data isolation: tenant-level isolation and dedicated network/VPC required for PII-derived models.
- Predictable throughput: need 50–80 concurrent inference streams for real-time triage at peak.
- Latency SLO: targeted 95th percentile < 150ms for 512-token requests; cold-starts must be mitigated.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + evidence of audit logs and key management integration (KMS/HSM).

What we proposed on the call (agreed next-closest architecture):
- Dedicated Reserved Pool: 8x A100-class GPUs (reserved) in a single VPC with private control plane.
- Isolation: model-serving only on dedicated nodes; optional network-level isolation and customer-managed KMS.
- Scaling plan: baseline reserved capacity (8 GPUs) with burst pool for up to +50% for scheduled peaks; autoscaling policy with warm standby and instant failover to a fallback model for graceful degradation.
- SLA targets: 99.5% uptime for the Dedicated cluster; p95 token latency target <= 150ms for configured request sizes; documented escalation path and runbook.

Attachments: medai-mrp-requirements.pdf (your MRP notes) and redwood-dedicated-proposal.xlsx (draft capacity + price bands).

Immediate next steps we agreed:
1) Redwood: produce a firm pricing proposal and committed capacity options (monthly and annual) — Evelyn to lead.
2) MedAI: share answers to the security questionnaire and confirm any additional network constraints (e.g., egress rules) — Samira / procurement.
3) Legal/procurement: request to review proposed contract term sheet; we can provide our standard enterprise addendum.
4) Pilot plan: 2-week canary using 2 reserved GPUs + routing policy to measure real latency under your traffic shape. If pilot passes, we expand to reserved pool.

Evelyn / Karthik — can you confirm: pricing tiers (monthly commit & 12-month commit delta), what the burst pricing looks like, and an estimated lead time to field the reserved pool? I will follow up with a tailored slide and the pilot runbook by EOD tomorrow.

Samira / Victor — anything I missed or any numbers you want adjusted in the proposal?

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas — thanks for the thorough recap. This matches our notes and is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 50–80 concurrent streams is a weekly peak estimate; our baseline is closer to 35 sustained during daytime. Please include both baseline and peak in the proposal.
- For the p95 <= 150ms, that target is for inference only (model -> token generation). Transcoding/serialization latency can be separate.
- Procurement asked that any reserved-commit contract include a 30-day ramp clause and a break clause tied to unmet SLA targets for the first 3 months.

We are uploading the completed security questionnaire today and want to schedule a short call with our infra team next week to discuss VPC peering and KMS integration. Victor will coordinate the time.

Attachments: MedAI_Security_Questionnaire_Feb19.pdf (will follow in a separate email).

Samira
